title: Parallel Data Loading
description: Speed up your Next.js pages by loading independent data in parallel using Promise.all and parallel route segments.

data.text: When a page needs multiple pieces of data, the order in which you load them matters. If you fetch them one after another, the total load time is the sum of every request. Parallel loading lets you start all requests at the same time and wait for them together, dramatically reducing wait time.

Next.js supports parallel loading at the framework level through route segments and Promise.all in Server Components. Understanding these patterns is essential for building fast, responsive full-stack applications.

By default, if you await multiple promises one after another in an async Server Component, each request waits for the previous one to finish. If your page needs a user profile, recent orders, and notifications, sequential fetching means the slowest request blocks everything else.

data.title: Sequential fetching — slow
data.content: Fetching data sequentially — each request waits for the previous one to complete.

data.text: Wrap independent promises in Promise.all to start them simultaneously. The component waits for all of them to resolve before rendering, but they all run at the same time. In the example above, the total time becomes the slowest single request, not the sum of all three.

data.title: Parallel fetching with Promise.all — fast
data.content: Fetching data in parallel with Promise.all — all requests start at the same time.

data.text: Next.js also supports parallel route segments using the @folder convention. Two or more slots in the same layout load independently and render simultaneously. This is especially useful for dashboards with multiple independent panels.

data.content: Parallel route segments in Next.js file-system routing.

data.title: Layout receiving parallel slots
data.content: A layout receiving two parallel slots and rendering them side by side.

data.text: One of the biggest benefits of parallel routes is that each slot can show its own loading state. Users see panels as they finish rather than waiting for the slowest panel. Combine parallel routes with loading.tsx files for instant, progressive dashboards.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Only use Promise.all for independent data. If one request depends on the result of another, sequential fetching is correct. Measure performance before and after to confirm the optimization helps real users.

data.title: Summary
points: Parallel data loading reduces total wait time by fetching independent data simultaneously.
Use Promise.all for parallel fetches in Server Components.
Parallel route segments let you build dashboard layouts with independent panels.
Each panel can stream in with its own loading state for a progressive experience.
